chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-At'tar narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: I asked Ar-Rida (peace be upon him)

about marrying women who have been divorced thrice. He said to me: 'Your triple divorce is not permissible for others, but their triple divorce is permissible for you, because you do not consider the triple divorce to be valid, while they consider yours to be valid.'

key_terms.لَا تَرَوْنَ الثَّلَاثَ شَيْئًا: you do not consider the triple divorce to be valid/effective

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on triple divorce compared to Sunni Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential divergence regarding triple divorce (talqah thalath) by attributing it to differing perceptions of validity: Shias do not regard the three pronouncements as immediately binding, whereas Sunnis do. This epistemological difference dictates the reciprocal permissibility of intermarriage; since Shias view the divorce as not final, the woman remains permissible to her husband, while Sunnis view it as final, making her permissible to others. This hadith highlights how shared religious practices can coexist with distinct legal interpretations without necessitating separation.
